_description: Shared fixture corpus for retrieval quality validation (T09). Contains realistic agent-work skills across Rust, Docker Compose, git, testing, and security. Used by tests/e2e and scripts/run-demo.sh to validate threshold alignment without artificial tuning.

_thresholds.note: These are the RetrievalConfig defaults. Positive fixtures must clear 0.20; negative fixtures must stay below it on a cold-start empty graph.

positive_fixtures.name: rust-tokio-async-file-io
positive_fixtures.description: Async file I/O patterns in Rust using tokio::fs — reading, writing, and error boundaries for async contexts

subunits.title: Read file with tokio::fs::read_to_string
subunits.content: Use tokio::fs::read_to_string for small files; prefer BufReader for large files to avoid loading the entire content into memory at once

subunits.title: Propagate IO errors with anyhow or thiserror
subunits.content: Wrap tokio::io::Error in a domain error type using thiserror; avoid unwrap at async file boundaries

positive_fixtures.roundtrip_prompt: how to read files in rust with tokio async
positive_fixtures.rationale: Highly lexical and semantic overlap: rust + tokio + async + file + read all appear in both skill and prompt

positive_fixtures.name: docker-compose-service-health
positive_fixtures.description: Docker Compose healthcheck patterns for Postgres, Redis, and Qdrant — wait-for-healthy sequencing in test environments

subunits.title: Add HEALTHCHECK to Compose services
subunits.content: Use condition: service_healthy in depends_on so dependent containers wait for the health probe to pass before starting

subunits.title: Use alpine pg_isready for Postgres health probes
subunits.content: HEALTHCHECK CMD pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB} -q is the canonical probe — avoids full connection overhead

positive_fixtures.roundtrip_prompt: docker compose healthcheck postgres redis wait for healthy
positive_fixtures.rationale: Strong lexical overlap on docker, compose, healthcheck, postgres, redis

positive_fixtures.name: git-conventional-commit-workflow
positive_fixtures.description: Conventional commit message format and git workflow for incremental feature development with trunk-based branching

subunits.title: Write a conventional commit message
subunits.content: Format: <type>(<scope>): <description>. Types: feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore. Scope is the affected crate or module.

subunits.title: Create feature branches from main
subunits.content: Branch from main, prefix with feat/, fix/, or docs/. Rebase before merge to keep a linear history.

positive_fixtures.roundtrip_prompt: git commit message format conventional commits feature branch
positive_fixtures.rationale: Direct lexical match on git, commit, conventional, branch

positive_fixtures.name: rust-unit-testing-patterns
positive_fixtures.description: Rust unit and integration testing patterns — test module structure, assertion helpers, and test-only feature gates

subunits.title: Inline test module with #[cfg(test)]
subunits.content: Place unit tests in a #[cfg(test)] mod tests block at the bottom of the source file. Use #[test] for sync and #[tokio::test] for async tests.

subunits.title: Use test-utils feature gate for integration test helpers
subunits.content: Expose test-only types and constructors behind a cfg(feature = 'test-utils') gate so production builds are never polluted.

positive_fixtures.roundtrip_prompt: rust unit test async tokio test module structure
positive_fixtures.rationale: Semantic overlap on rust + testing + async + tokio

positive_fixtures.name: security-secrets-management
positive_fixtures.description: Secrets management patterns for agent-based systems — environment variables, never-log rules, and secret rotation without restart

subunits.title: Never log secrets or credentials
subunits.content: Secrets sourced from env vars must not appear in tracing spans or error messages. Use #[tracing::instrument(skip(secret))] to suppress secret fields.

subunits.title: Rotate secrets without restart using env reload
subunits.content: Trigger a secret reload by watching a signal (SIGHUP) or a Redis pub/sub message; reload the env var in the hot path without stopping the server.

positive_fixtures.roundtrip_prompt: how to manage secrets credentials security env variables
positive_fixtures.rationale: Semantic and lexical match on secrets, credentials, security, env

negative_fixtures.prompt: how to make a cappuccino with an espresso machine
negative_fixtures.rationale: Completely unrelated to agent-work skills. An empty graph or a skills graph with only Rust/Docker/git content must return no_match for this prompt.

negative_fixtures.prompt: what is the capital of france
negative_fixtures.rationale: General knowledge question with zero overlap with any agent-work skill in the corpus. Proves the threshold gate is not trivially passed.
